comment.narrative: At least 6

Aimag General Land Management Plan serves as a guide for the development and enforcement of Soum Territorial Development Plans where its principles and concepts are incorporated and is aligned with the Land Laws State general land management plans and other legal documents. Soum Territorial Development Plans serve as crucial midterm documents for effective land administration and land resource management within the entire soum territory and is a basic document for the development of soum annual land management plans. Hence these interrelated policy and planning documents are underway to be approved by respective aimag and soum Citizens Representative Khurals. As part of the feasibility required for a draft of amendments to the Law on Land the GoM organized consultation meetings in different regions based on a participatory approach. According to legislators the expected amendment intends to improve the legal environment of pastureland to ensure decreased land degradations and a reduced rate of desertification throughout the country. The consultation meeting for the central region of Mongolia was organized in Darkhan with the required support and project involvement. During the meeting the draft lawmakers and relevant working groups presented ongoing concepts of potential law amendments to local communities and got comments from the officials and the publiclocal herders. Over 60 participants including MPs aimag and soum governors local officers herders and farmers were involved in the meeting and provided the required comments to make the draft more sophisticated. The comments will be reflected in the other formulation process of draft amendments for submission to Parliament.

description.narrative: 1.2 Indicator 1: of agroecological product value chains developed

comment.narrative: At least 2 products per soum six soums total 12 products.

Artificial insemination was practised for 452 cows through the Red Angus breed with fast growths and conception rate was 77 in average and 558 sheep through Altai breeds and conception rate was 73 in average respectively. To enhance livestock quality a Livestock breeding centre was established in cooperation with the Governors office Euruu soum of Selenge aimag and the required set of equipment was supplied by the project. Practical training on the innovative use of electrocautery castration was organized involving relevant livestock specialists and herders of target soums. Electrocautery castration technique was applied with the involvement of local livestock experts and herders to over 50 young cattle to ensure early economic circulation and enhance growth.To ensure local protein and mineral fodder resources for livestock a factory with a capacity to manufacture 9001000kg of salt mineral block per hour was established in Khurkh Umnudelger soum As a result of project support to diversify recipes of concentrated feeds nine different types of concentrated feeds were prepared and recommended for production. A total of over 20 tons of products in two types were produced and delivered to local consumers and stakeholders with positive feedback. In order to ensure improved livestock health two livestock dipping facilities were established in the Yeruu soum of Selenge aimag and BayanAdarga Khentii aimag following the standards with specific environmental safeguard requirements developed and approved by the GAVS.Within the framework of developing dairy value chains artificial insemination was applied for 50 cows of 2 households by Simmental breed and two local specialists were involved and specialized in artificial insemination techniques at the site. This ensures an increased winter milk supply. The diversity of local dairy products were increased by 5 new products including milk with honey yogurt sour cream vanilla curd and sour drink following the project support to establishment of small dairy plant and dairy trainings.

Women herders group operating in Binder soum were identified as the most potential stakeholder and women members were involved in a series of trainings. As a result their capacity was significantly enhanced regarding the use of required techniques for innovative dairy products. A smallscale milk processing unit with a capacity to produce 80100 lday was established by costsharing principles. 35 products are being supplied to the Lunch program and over 400 students of primary school in Binder soum are benefitting from the development of the dairy value chain. To develop a meat value chain in BayanAdarga Binder and Umnudelger soums of Khentii aimag the project plans to start conducting artificial insemination for 600 cows from 50 households in 3 soums. Preliminary studies have been carried out. In cooperation with a cooperative PIU has conducted relevant studies to establish an intersoum livestock feed mill unit for 3 soums of Khentii aimag as a pilot demonstration of the fodder value chain. The unit with a capacity to produce 16 tonnes of fodder per day will be based in Umnudelger soum. For the reporting period the project focused on the improvement of veterinary service livestock health issues as well as animal productivity. In this scope blueprints and technical specifications for the establishment of small ruminant dipping facilities were initiated in 2 soums including the Eruu soum of Selenge aimag and the BayanAdarga soum of Khentii aimag. As a result 110 households with over 45000 animals are expected to use the dipping facility which will be established in line with applicable National new standards and associated environmental safeguard requirements.

The trainers are expected to work at 9 districts of the capital and 330 soums of 21 aimags reaching throughout the country. Under the guidance of MET and professional oversight of the Forestry Institute a Manual with more than 500 pages B5 was created and published with the involvement of over 60 promising professors for reference for national trainers and farmers. In cooperation with MULS Potential possibilities to develop agroforestry system with a scientific basis conference is being carried out where preliminary results of agroforestry experiments carried out in the Nart research station of the university. Participants were provided with a better understanding of the scientific basis for agroforestry systems and their practical applications in terms of climate change adaptations.

title.narrative: Indicator 1: of climate and environmentally friendly value chains that support food system

description.narrative: Indicator 1: of climate and environmentally friendly value chains that support food system

comment.narrative: At least two value chains

The project continues to develop value chains based on agroecological principles. In order to improve the balance between plants animals people and the environment it is necessary to reduce the number of livestock to ensure the restoration and sustainability of the grassland ecosystem without having a negative influence to the sustainable income generation for herders. Hence the project focused on increasing the income of herders improving the breed of cattle and sheep and reducing the number of cattle and sheep by the herd structure optimizations in 3 target soums of Khentii aimag and in Yeruu soum of Selenge aimag under beef and mutton value chain. Within the framework of developing dairy value chains artificial insemination was applied for 50 cows of 2 households by Simmental breed and two local specialists were involved and specialized in artificial insemination techniques at the site. This ensures an increased winter milk supply. With the project support the milk processing unit which initially had the capacity to process 100 litres of milk per day has been expanded to handle 1000 liters of milk daily. As a result the range of local dairy products has been diversified with the introduction of five new products.

title.narrative: Indicator 3: of local fairs to promote agroecological value chains

description.narrative: Indicator 3: of local fairs to promote agroecological value chains

comment.narrative: At least one in each aimag total two.

Three events have been organized by project to promote agroecological value chainsAn international conference Importance of Geographical Indication was organized in September 2022 in cooperation with the EU Ministry of Justice and Home Affairs MOJHA and Intellectual Property Office of Mongolia IPOM. As part of the GI the project identified 23 potential local GI products including black cherry sour cream Eruu honey and Khurkh barley flour and focused on the further process for product development. More than 200 participants agreed on the importance of GI significant ways and further roadmaps to develop GI in Mongolia ensuring public and private sectors. The AgroecologySustainable Agriculture International scientific conference was organized in November 2022 in cooperation with the Mongolian University of Life Science MULS and the Embassy of the Republic of Poland in Mongolia. Participants shared international and national level scientific achievements on agroecology and sustainable agriculture experience including implementation of agroecological and sustainable development principles knowledge of advances achievements best practices and challenges and solutions in the socioeconomic crop production livestock and forestry sectors. A national conference Potential possibilities to develop agroforestry system with a scientific basis was organized in cooperation with the School of Agroecology MULS in April 2023. Participants shared knowledge and experience on scientific basis for agroforestry systems and their practical applications in terms of climate change adaptations and how to establish silviculture and silvopastoral systems depending on local landscape specifics including ecological conditions climate soil fertility and selection of proper tree species to ensure sustainable and secured food systems and resilient ecosystems.
